turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have until 4:40, so let's not spend it on pleasantries. My son found out he had a zero on his phone, in the middle of class, and nobody called me first, so start with who decided that.
Thanks for coming in. I owe you an apology: the zero went in before I called you.
Okay. That's procedure 4.2, and I'm writing down that you've just admitted it wasn't followed. Now, on what basis was the zero entered at all?
I am withdrawing the zero today. Owen does a private supervised rewrite at lunch. Nothing goes on his record. I will email you that tonight.

Zero withdrawn today, nothing on his record, in writing tonight; I'm writing that down. But a rewrite means you still have a concern about Owen's essay, and you haven't shown me one thing behind it. What do you actually have, Hale, beyond a machine's guess?
Here it is in writing, signed.

I'll read it properly before I say anything about it. If it says what you just told me, zero withdrawn, private, nothing on file, then I want the principal copied on it tonight. And I'm still waiting to hear why Owen is rewriting anything at all.
Thank you for your time, Ms. Kalinowski.

We're not finished, Hale. You've given me terms, but you haven't given me a reason Owen should sit a rewrite instead of just having his mark restored. Answer that, or I'm walking down to the principal's office with this paper in my hand.
"Goodbye." Okay. Then I'm taking your signed page to the principal's office now, and I'll be asking why Owen is rewriting an essay nobody has shown me a single reason to doubt.
